_comment: nadia as an ECS task on Fargate — one task, one agent run.
Replace ACCOUNT, REGION and the two role ARNs, then:
aws ecs run-task --cluster CLUSTER --task-definition nadia --launch-type FARGATE \
The task text is a command override rather than a baked-in argument, so one registered
definition serves every task instead of a new revision per run.
KNOWN GAP, stated here because it decides how you configure this: nadia authenticates to
Bedrock with a Bedrock API key (a bearer token), not with SigV4 against the task role.
That means the key has to exist as a secret, and the task role is NOT what grants model
access. SigV4 is the native AWS answer and it is not implemented — see BACKLOG NAD-12.
ECS injects secrets as environment variables only; there is no file projection as there
is in Kubernetes. So on ECS the credential arrives in the environment, which the agent's
child processes inherit. That is a real difference in posture from the k8s manifests, and
it is the reason --api-key-file exists and is preferred where it can be used.
